canDo.en: I can describe a problem, make a polite complaint, and give advice with should, ought to and "If I were you…".
canDo.bg: Мога да опиша проблем, да направя учтиво оплакване и да дам съвет със should, ought to и "If I were you…".

title.en: Giving advice: should, ought to, If I were you
title.bg: Съвети: should, ought to, If I were you

body.en: "Should" + base verb is the most common way to give advice: You should see a doctor. "Ought to" means the same but is a little more formal: You ought to see a doctor. The negative is "shouldn't". "If I were you, I'd…" is softer and more personal. Use "were" for all persons here (If I were you, not normally "If I was you" in careful English). Never put "to" after "should": "You should to go" is wrong.
body.bg: "Should" + основна форма е най-честият начин да дадеш съвет: You should see a doctor (Трябва да отидеш на лекар). "Ought to" значи същото, но е малко по-официално: You ought to see a doctor. Отрицанието е "shouldn't". "If I were you, I'd…" (На твое място бих…) е по-меко и по-лично. Тук се използва "were" за всички лица (If I were you, а в грижлив английски не "If I was you"). След "should" никога не слагай "to": "You should to go" е грешно.

examples: You shouldn't drink coffee so late.
You ought to talk to your manager.
If I were you, I'd look for a new job.

body.en: In English a direct complaint can sound aggressive, so people usually soften it. Start with "I'm afraid…" or "I'm sorry to bother you, but…", describe the problem, and ask with "Could you…?" or "Would you mind + -ing…?". In Bulgarian a direct "Музиката ви е много силна" is often fine, but in English "Your music is too loud" alone can start a conflict.
body.bg: На английски прякото оплакване може да прозвучи агресивно, затова обикновено се смекчава. Започни с "I'm afraid…" или "I'm sorry to bother you, but…", опиши проблема и помоли с "Could you…?" или "Would you mind + -ing…?". На български прякото "Музиката ви е много силна" често е нормално, но на английски само "Your music is too loud" може да предизвика конфликт.

texts.title: Noisy neighbours
paragraphs: Dimitar wrote: I moved into a new flat in March, and at first everything was fine. But my new neighbours play loud music almost every night, often until two in the morning. I've knocked on their door twice, but nothing has changed. I'm exhausted and I have exams next month. What should I do?
Kate replied: That sounds awful. If I were you, I'd write them a short, polite note. Some people honestly don't realise how thin the walls are.
Marco replied: You ought to keep a record of the dates and times. If it doesn't stop, you should contact the building manager. I wouldn't call the police yet, though — it might make things worse.

items.sentence: You look really tired. You ___ go to bed earlier.

explanation.en: The most common word for advice is "should" + base verb ("ought to" is a little more formal). No "to" after "should". "Had better", "must" and "need to" are also possible here, but they sound stronger — more like a warning than friendly advice.
explanation.bg: Най-честата дума за съвет е "should" + основна форма ("ought to" е малко по-официално). След "should" няма "to". "Had better", "must" и "need to" също са възможни тук, но звучат по-силно — по-скоро като предупреждение, отколкото като приятелски съвет.

items.prompt: Which piece of advice is grammatically correct?

explanation.en: "Should" is followed directly by the base verb: should call. "Ought" needs "to": ought to call. In Bulgarian you say "трябва да", and that "да" makes learners add "to" after "should".
explanation.bg: След "should" идва директно основната форма: should call. "Ought" изисква "to": ought to call. На български казваш "трябва да" и това "да" кара учащите да слагат "to" след "should".

hints.bg: След "should" никога няма "to". След "ought" винаги има.

objective.en: Give advice with "If I were you".
objective.bg: Да дадеш съвет с "If I were you".

accept: If I were you, I'd apologise.

explanation.en: "If I were you, I'd…" is an unreal (second) conditional: you are not the other person, so we use the past form "were" and then "would" ('d) + base verb. It's like Bulgarian "На твое място бих се извинил".
explanation.bg: "If I were you, I'd…" е нереално (второ) условно изречение: ти не си другият човек, затова използваме миналата форма "were" и после "would" ('d) + основна форма. Като "На твое място бих се извинил".

items.sentence: If I ___ you, I wouldn't lend him any more money.

explanation.en: In this fixed phrase we use the past form because the situation is imaginary — I am not you. "Were" is the standard form in careful English; "was" is common in informal speech, so it is accepted too.
explanation.bg: В този устойчив израз използваме минала форма, защото ситуацията е въображаема — аз не съм ти. "Were" е стандартната форма в грижлив английски; "was" е често в неформална реч, затова също се приема.

hints.en: The situation is imaginary, so the verb goes into the past.
hints.bg: Ситуацията е въображаема, затова глаголът е в минало.

items.prompt: Complete the advice: "If you spoke to your boss, she ___ understand."

explanation.en: "If + past simple" (spoke) describes an imagined situation, so the other half needs "would": she would understand. "Will" goes with the present in the if-part (If you speak…, she will…).
explanation.bg: "If + past simple" (spoke) описва въображаема ситуация, затова втората част изисква "would": she would understand. "Will" върви със сегашно време в if-частта (If you speak…, she will…).

hints.en: Look at the verb after "If": it's in the past.
hints.bg: Виж глагола след "If": в минало е.

items.prompt: Your soup in a restaurant is cold. Which is the most natural and polite thing to say to the waiter?
options: Your soup is cold. Bring another.
I'm afraid my soup is cold. Could you warm it up, please?
I want a hot soup now.

explanation.en: "I'm afraid…" softens the bad news and "Could you…, please?" makes a polite request. The two direct demands are grammatically fine but sound rude in English, and "Why you bring cold soup?" is not correct English.
explanation.bg: "I'm afraid…" смекчава лошата новина, а "Could you…, please?" е учтива молба. Двете директни искания са граматически верни, но звучат грубо на английски, а "Why you bring cold soup?" не е правилен английски.

hints.en: Look for a softener at the start and a polite question.
hints.bg: Потърси смекчаваща фраза в началото и учтив въпрос.

items.sentence: Would you mind ___ (turn) the music down a little?

explanation.en: After "Would you mind" we use the -ing form: Would you mind turning…? Not "to turn". It literally asks "Would it bother you…?", so the polite answer if you agree is "No, not at all."
explanation.bg: След "Would you mind" използваме -ing форма: Would you mind turning…? Не "to turn". Буквално пита "Ще те притесни ли…?", затова учтивият отговор, ако си съгласен, е "No, not at all."

objective.en: Understand the main problem in a forum post.
objective.bg: Да разбереш основния проблем в публикация във форум.

items.prompt: Why is Dimitar especially worried about the noise?
options: He has exams soon and can't sleep.
The neighbours are rude to him.

explanation.en: He writes: "I'm exhausted and I have exams next month." The text doesn't mention work, a baby, or rude neighbours.
explanation.bg: Той пише: "I'm exhausted and I have exams next month." В текста не се споменават работа, бебе или груби съседи.

hints.en: Read the end of Dimitar's post.
hints.bg: Прочети края на публикацията на Dimitar.

objective.en: Understand advice and reasons in a reply.
objective.bg: Да разбереш съвет и причина в отговор.

items.prompt: What does Marco think about calling the police?
options: It isn't a good idea yet, because it could make the situation worse.
It's the first thing Dimitar should do.
The police won't come for noise.
Kate should do it, not Dimitar.

explanation.en: Marco says: "I wouldn't call the police yet, though — it might make things worse." "I wouldn't…" is another way to give advice: it means "don't do it".
explanation.bg: Marco казва: "I wouldn't call the police yet, though — it might make things worse." "I wouldn't…" е още един начин да дадеш съвет: значи "не го прави".

items.sentence: Kate thinks Dimitar should write the neighbours a polite ___.

explanation.en: Kate writes: "If I were you, I'd write them a short, polite note."
explanation.bg: Kate пише: "If I were you, I'd write them a short, polite note."

hints.en: Read Kate's reply. What should Dimitar write?
hints.bg: Прочети отговора на Kate. Какво да напише Dimitar?
